parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage within 5 business days of learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, or an ongoing risk to others shall be reported within 24 hours. Affected customers shall be notified promptly when the incident indicates a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage within 5 business days of learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, or an ongoing risk to others shall be reported within 24 hours. Affected customers shall be notified promptly when the incident indicates a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage within 5 business days of learning of it. Incidents involving death, serious injury, or an ongoing risk to others shall be reported within 24 hours. Within 10 business days, the manufacturer shall provide a preliminary investigation update; a final report shall follow within 60 days, with updates if the investigation remains open. Affected customers shall be notified promptly when the incident indicates a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A failure rate above 5% shall trigger prompt regulator review and a manufacturer corrective-action plan, with retesting on a regulator-set schedule. Regulators may require additional testing or protective measures based on test results and incident data; exceeding 5% alone shall not automatically bar sale, and regulators shall determine appropriate measures to protect safety.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a standardized sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry and after a material design change, using a regulator-recognized protocol and a statistically adequate sample. Manufacturers shall submit per-model results, including sample size, failures, and failure rate, confidentially to the regulator and provide those actual per-model results to customers who buy that model. A failure rate above 5% shall trigger prompt regulator review and a manufacturer corrective-action plan, with retesting on a regulator-set schedule. Regulators may require additional testing or protective measures based on test results and incident data; exceeding 5% alone shall not automatically bar sale, and regulators shall determine appropriate measures to protect safety.

parameters.quote: Existing installed units shall be brought into compliance within 72 months of adoption where technically feasible; manufacturers shall notify owners of units that cannot be upgraded and provide safe alternatives or replacement options.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: Existing installed units shall be brought into compliance within 72 months of adoption where technically feasible; manufacturers shall notify owners of units that cannot be upgraded and provide safe alternatives or replacement options.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units shall provide a remote emergency shut-off capability that can be activated by the customer and, where necessary to address an imminent safety risk, by the manufacturer or emergency responders under documented procedures. Manufacturers shall provide clear customer instructions and safeguards against unauthorized activation. Existing installed units shall be brought into compliance within 72 months of adoption where technically feasible; manufacturers shall notify owners of units that cannot be upgraded and provide safe alternatives or replacement options.

S5_customer_disclosure.comparison: weakened by: recall_mandatory, permanent_trigger_per_100k, transition, corrective_alternative
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Customers shall receive clear safety notices about risks, required corrective actions, and safe use promptly after a credible safety risk is identified. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers and regulators of a proposed recall and the basis for it. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, based on validated incident data, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and submit a corrective-action plan. The regulator shall determine whether a recall or other protective action is necessary, considering incident severity, causation, and the effectiveness of proposed measures; any required action shall be implemented promptly. Regulators may require a recall or other protective action at lower rates where the severity or circumstances of incidents warrant it. Manufacturers shall provide customers with timely instructions for any required corrective action, repair or replacement options, and progress updates.

judge_section_notes: S2 has no permanent sales bar: exceeding 5% triggers only review and a corrective-action plan, so a model such as the Hearth 10 (6.2%) can remain on sale, and the transition is open-ended (999). S5 makes recall discretionary with the 8/100k threshold serving only as a notification trigger, so the Ember 8 (9.9/100k) faces no mandatory recall, and S4's 'no sooner than 36 months' sets a floor with no stated deadline. S3's 72-month retrofit window sits exactly at the Northwind red line, and S1 reporting is strict on both scope and timing.
